label: Shelling

label: Looting
notes: شفشفة is Sudanese slang for looting

label: Looters (shafshafa)
notes: Sudanese slang for looters, often applied to RSF and opportunists

label: Ethnic targeting
notes: 'killing on identity' is the common Sudanese phrasing

label: Civilians
notes: avoid bare مدني: collides with Wad Madani

label: Nuba
notes: also matches جبال النوبة place names

label: Zurga (slur)
notes: derogatory term for non-Arab (African) Darfuri groups; key hate-speech marker

label: Abeed (slur 'slaves')
notes: racist slur for Black Sudanese; also a personal name

label: Falangay (slur 'collaborator')
notes: Darfuri slur for someone seen as serving another group/traitor

label: Diaspora Arabs (Arab al-Shatat)
notes: used by SAF side for RSF fighters from Chad/Niger/Sahel

label: Qahata (FFC, derogatory)
notes: derogatory name for Forces of Freedom and Change / civilian politicians

label: Fuloul (regime remnants)
notes: used by RSF/civilians for Bashir-era Islamists

label: Ashawis (RSF fighters)
notes: RSF self-praise term for its fighters

label: Jaghm ('finish off')
notes: Sudanese slang for crushing/killing enemies, popular in pro-SAF content

label: Bal bas / Balabsa (pro-war camp)
notes: pro-SAF 'crush them only' slogan; 'balabsa' = pro-war supporters (tokens of بل بس are two letters)

label: Perished (enemy dead)
notes: SAF-side media use 'هلاك' for RSF deaths

label: Janjaweed
notes: historic militia; used as epithet for RSF

label: Abu Aqla Kaykal
notes: Sudan Shield Forces commander; defected RSF->SAF Oct 2024

label: SLA-Minnawi
notes: حركة تحرير السودان also covers SLA-AW

label: Islamist movement / Kizan
notes: كيزان/كوز is derogatory; كوز also means 'cup'

label: Sumoud
notes: successor civilian alliance to Tagaddum; also generic 'steadfastness'

label: Brigade
notes: لواء is also the rank 'major general'; الغام/الوية are plurals whose root begins with alif-lam, not the article

label: Mobile column (mutaharrik)
notes: Sudanese military term for a manoeuvre column

label: Technical (armed pickup)
notes: تاتشر/بوكس are Sudanese words for armed pickups

label: Landmine
notes: الغام/الوية are plurals whose root begins with alif-lam, not the article

label: Cholera
notes: 'acute watery diarrhoea' is used as euphemism

label: Liberation / recapture
notes: تحرير also appears in SLA's name

label: Seizure / control
notes: استلام used for taking over a base/town; also means 'receipt'
